description: Sync customers, invoices, subscriptions and charges from one Stripe account. Invoices, subscriptions and charges link to their customer.
opening: Sync customers, invoices, subscriptions and charges from one Stripe account. Each record is one document with a readable summary, and an invoice carries its line items. Invoices, subscriptions and charges link to their customer.

Stripe permissions are not imported, so every synced record is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Other Stripe objects, such as products, refunds and payouts, are not synced. Deletions in Stripe are not detected.

opening.text: Searchable amounts assume two decimal places. For a currency such as JPY, an amount of 100 is shown as 1.00, so the searchable text understates it by a factor of 100. Original stored amounts are unchanged.

connect.auth: Stripe uses a secret key together with the account id.

credentials.name: client_secret
credentials.text: A Stripe secret key, `sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`, with read access to the account's resources.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the secret key as `client_secret` and the account id as `account_id`.

steps.title: Select the account
steps.text: Select the account's `All data` resource. It syncs customers, invoices, subscriptions and charges together. You cannot select these record types separately.

connect.account: One connector reads one Stripe account. A test-mode key reads test data and a live-mode key reads live data.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync lists records created in the sync window, and reads Stripe's events for updates in the same window.
sync.edits: An update, such as an invoice being paid, arrives as an event and replaces the record's document.
sync.deletes: Deletions in Stripe are not detected. A deleted record stays in HydraDB.
notes: Updates are read from events that reach back 30 days. After a long pause, updates to older records can be missed.

shared_attributes.name: created
shared_attributes.text: When the record was created. It stays the result date after the record is updated, so ranking by date follows creation time. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.stripe_id
shared_attributes.text: The Stripe id: `cus_...`, `in_...`, `sub_...` or `ch_...`. Targets one record. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's records. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: Other Stripe fields
shared_attributes.text: Every other field Stripe returns for the record, such as a customer's address, metadata or invoice settings. Kept for inspection only. A query does not match them and cannot filter on them.

documents.name: Customers
documents.title: The customer's name, or their email when there is no name.
documents.text: The customer's description, then `Name`, `Email`, `Phone` and `Balance` lines, with the balance in its currency. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: email
attributes.text: The customer's email. It identifies the customer as a person in the graph, appears in the `Email` line, and is the title when there is no name.

documents.name: Invoices
documents.one_document: One invoice, with its line items.
documents.title: `Invoice <number> - <customer>`, using the customer's name or email.
documents.text: The invoice description, then `Customer`, `Email`, `Status`, `Total`, `Amount due`, `Amount paid`, `Due date` and `Line items` lines. Each line item shows its description and amount. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: Line items
attributes.text: Each line's description and amount, written into the `Line items` line.

attributes.name: customer
attributes.text: The customer id. Links the invoice to its customer. The id itself is not searchable. The customer's name or email is part of the text.

documents.name: Subscriptions
documents.title: The plan's nickname or name, or the plan id, followed by `subscription`.
documents.text: `Plan`, `Status`, `Amount`, `Quantity`, `Customer`, `Started` and `Current period end` lines. `Amount` is the plan price with its currency and interval, for example `49.00 USD/month`. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: plan
attributes.text: The plan nickname or name, or the plan id when neither is available, forms the title followed by `subscription`. Its price and billing interval form the searchable `Amount` line. Product or price details that live only in other fields are not searchable.

attributes.name: customer
attributes.text: The customer id links the subscription to its customer. The searchable `Customer` line uses the customer's name when known, or the id otherwise.

documents.name: Charges
documents.title: The charge description, or `Charge <amount currency> - <customer>` when there is none.
documents.text: The charge description, then `Customer`, `Amount`, `Status`, `Receipt email` and `Failure message` lines. `Customer` is the first of the billing name, billing email, receipt email, customer name and customer id that is present. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: customer
attributes.text: The customer id. Links the charge to its customer. The id itself is not searchable unless it is the only customer detail, in which case it fills the `Customer` line.

example_searches: What status, amount due and amount paid are recorded for Acme Corp's invoice INV-0042?
What plan is jane@example.com subscribed to, and when does the current period end?
Why did the charge for jane@example.com fail?

connections: Charges are not linked to their invoice, and invoices are not linked to their subscription.
people: Each customer, identified by their email.
graph.from_text: Descriptions, plan names and the rest of each record's summary.

not_synced: Products, prices and plans as their own documents.
Events, payouts, refunds, disputes, balance transactions and other Stripe objects.
Invoice PDFs and hosted invoice pages.
